chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad al-Hannat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'No one is given from the zakat less than five dirhams, and this is the minimum that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, prescribed for zakat in the wealth of Muslims, so do not give anyone less than five dirhams and upwards.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of zakat that should be given to an individual recipient according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing five dirhams as the minimum threshold for zakat distribution to a single recipient, linking this specific amount to the general minimum prescribed by Allah for zakat on wealth. This ruling ensures that the administrative burden of collecting and distributing small amounts does not outweigh the benefit to the recipient, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt. The emphasis on 'five dirhams' serves as a distinct legal boundary for the validity of the gift within the broader framework of zakat obligations.
